STEP 1 - Scene: A snack-style plate of fresh fruit: red grapes and one whole green-yellow pear (or similar fruit) on a white square plate. Photographed from directly above (top-down view), so the plate's width is undistorted.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate, roughly 22 cm across the side (the plate spans about 2/3 of the frame height, consistent with a side plate). Treat as a ~22 cm square; the plate is roughly 20 cm wide by 22 cm, so area ≈ 400 cm² (rounded-square estimate).

STEP 3 - Items: (1) red seedless grapes, about 16 small grapes, each ~2 cm diameter; (2) one whole pear, roughly 8 cm diameter and 9 cm tall, green-yellow skin.

STEP 4 - Area: Grapes cluster covers roughly 12% of plate area (~48 cm²). Pear covers roughly 13% (~52 cm²). Total food ≈ 25% of plate, which is consistent with a light snack.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Grapes: cluster of ~48 cm² footprint, height ~2 cm → ~96 ml gross.
- Pear: whole fruit, ~8 cm diameter sphere-ish, volume ≈ (4/3)π(4)³ ≈ 268 ml (use ~250 ml with slight flattening).

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Grapes: 96 ml × 0.6 ≈ 58 g. Sanity check: 16 grapes × ~5 g ≈ 80 g, so use ~70 g.
- Pear: whole fruit ~250 ml × 0.9 (dense solid, but this is a whole piece, so use fruit density near 0.9 rather than the cut-piece bulk value) ≈ 230 g. A medium pear weighs roughly 170–200 g, so take ~180 g as the better estimate.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Grapes: 70 g × 69 kcal/100 g ≈ 48 kcal.
- Pear: 180 g × 57 kcal/100 g ≈ 103 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A small plate with 16 grapes and one medium pear totals about 250 g and about 150 kcal. This is plausible for a light fruit snack and does not assume a large serving.

Total: ~250 g, ~150 kcal.
